nodes.label: incident_key
nodes.rationale: Stable id for one alert across its lifecycle; the cab UI uses it to attach agent replies to the right alert.

nodes.label: SSE Event Stream (GET /api/stream)
nodes.rationale: Simplest delivery option; needs no public URL.

nodes.label: LangGraph Operator Agent
nodes.rationale: Kept outside this repo (not in requirements.txt) and connected over HTTP (event stream/webhook in, agent messages out), so it can be built against sample events without the simulator; a mock agent stands in until the real graph is connected.

nodes.label: De-duplicate Step
nodes.rationale: Reply once per incident_key on open, again on escalated, and at most every 10 min for update to avoid flooding the operator.

nodes.label: Route Step (category + severity)
nodes.rationale: Critical safety events take a fast path: short imperative message with speak: true.

nodes.label: Task Time Estimation Model
nodes.rationale: Trained on 5,000 simulated tasks; ~7% error versus ~30% for the planner's rule of thumb.

nodes.label: Hidden Ground Truth
nodes.rationale: Recorded by the simulator but withheld from detectors; it is what allows ML detection rate, lead time and false alarms to be measured objectively.

nodes.label: L3 ML Pattern (Residual-based Health Models)
nodes.rationale: Regression models learn what each signal should read for current load, rpm, ambient and warm-up; persistent residuals flag degradation and suggest a cause, catching radiator fouling ~2 h before the fixed alarm and injector wear that thresholds never catch.

nodes.label: Physics-based Construction Site Simulator
nodes.rationale: The provided sample datasets (Data.csv, IIoT set) are sparse, randomly ordered or label-noise, so temporal behaviour cannot be learned from them. The simulator encodes causal physics (load drives heat, clogging reduces cooling, fatigue makes controls jerkier) and records hidden ground truth so ML detection rate, lead time and false alarms can be measured rather than claimed.

nodes.label: Data.csv Sample Dataset
nodes.rationale: Sparse, randomly ordered readings; used only for plausible value ranges, not for training temporal models.

nodes.label: Detection Layer (Rules + ML)
nodes.rationale: Detectors never see hidden simulator state; every alert is detected from telemetry alone. The layer only consumes the telemetry dict and the plan, so a real machine can be mapped onto the same channel names and retrained with nothing downstream changing.

nodes.label: IIoT Sample Dataset
nodes.rationale: Independent noise with labels that look random; rejected as a training source.

nodes.label: Cause-Injection Scenarios (No Scripted Alerts)
nodes.rationale: Scenarios inject only causes (radiator clogging, surveyor behind counterweight, transmission failure, skipped warm-up) so that every alert must be genuinely detected from telemetry, proving the detection layer rather than scripting its output.

nodes.label: Enrich Step
nodes.rationale: Call tools only when needed to keep responses fast.

nodes.label: Idle Cause Attribution
nodes.rationale: Idle is attributed to truck wait, operator or unattended machine so fleet problems are surfaced to dispatch rather than blamed on the operator.

nodes.label: L5 Contextual Alerts
nodes.rationale: The same reading means different things in different situations (seatbelt off while digging is critical, while parked is info; idle due to truck breakdown is not the operator's fault).
